content: Dipeptidyl peptidase IV (DPP4), also known as aspartyl aminopeptidase, is an enzyme in humans that is encoded by the DNPEP gene. The protein encoded by the DNPEP gene functions as an aminopeptidase, which exhibits a preference for acidic amino acids. Specifically, it demonstrates a higher affinity for aspartic acid compared to glutamic acid. This enzyme is believed to be a cytosolic protein that plays a role in the general metabolism of intracellular proteins. To study the function of DNPEP, model organisms have been utilized. A conditional knockout mouse line, referred to as Dnpeptm1e(EUCOMM)Wtsi, was developed at the Wellcome Trust Sanger Institute. Both male and female mice from this line underwent a standardized phenotypic screening process to assess the effects of gene deletion.
